In other scenarios, set this parameter as needed.
item.name: dataType

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum number of backups that need to be retained for a single scheduled periodic backup task. When the total number of backups of all periodic tasks reaches the maximum number of allowed backups, the earliest backups are cleared. If this parameter is set to a non-zero value, the parameter value indicates the minimum number of backups that need to be retained for a scheduled periodic backup task. If this parameter is set to 0, there is no limit on the minimum number of backups. In this case, the backups are sorted by time and may be cleared at any time and are counted in the total number of backups.

item.name: enable

item.desc: This parameter sets the tolerance time for link disconnection (in minutes) of the fault protection function. When the link between an NE and the UME system is disconnected because the NE configuration parameters are modified, if the link between the NE and the UME cannot be reestablished within the time configured by this parameter, the NE automatically rolls back the configuration data to the status before the modification. If the system provides the reset self-rescue policy, the tolerance time for link disconnection (BrmFailsafe.brokenTolerantTime) of the fault protection function must be less than or equal to the result of the island self-rescue waiting time (IsletPolicy.isletRescueMins) of the reset self-rescue policy minus 10.
item.name: brokenTolerantTime

If the paraType parameter is set to 612, 746 or 842, the unit of this parameter is seconds and its value is in the range of 1 through 65535. If the paraType parameter is set to 634, the value is in the range of 1 through 65535. If the paraType parameter is set to 664, 677 or 760, the value is in the range of 1 through 4095. If the paraType parameter is set to 878, the value is in the range of 56 through 400. If the paraType parameter is set to 881, the value is in the range of 50 through 200. If the paraType parameter is set to 883, the value can be 0, 1, or 2. The value 0 indicates that the flow context aging function is disabled, 1 indicates that the flow aging time is reduced, and 2 indicates that the flow is deleted.

This function prevents that an alarm is automatically cleared repeatedly, which may cause it unable to be handled in a timely manner. In slight jitter mode, the threshold is set to 4 times in half of an hour. The enhance jitter mode is much stricter than slight jitter mode in the alarm jitter requirement.

item.desc: This parameter sets the allocation algorithm of energy consumption of each RAT. It is used to calculate the energy consumption of each RAT under the multimode base station.

item.desc: This parameter sets the NR power consumption percentage, which is used to calculate the power consumption KPI of the NR RAT. A multi-mode base station may use multiple RATs including NR, LTE, NB-IoT, UMTS, and GSM. The sum of power consumption percentage of each RAT is 100 %. The larger the power consumption percentage configured for a RAT is, the larger the power consumption KPI of this RAT is.
item.name: NRPercent

item.desc: This parameter sets the LTE power consumption percentage, which is used to calculate the power consumption KPI of the LTE RAT. A multi-mode base station may use multiple RATs including NR, LTE, NB-IoT, UMTS, and GSM. The sum of power consumption percentage of each RAT is 100 %. The larger the power consumption percentage configured for a RAT is, the larger the power consumption KPI of this RAT is.
item.name: LTEPercent

item.desc: This parameter sets the NB-IoT power consumption percentage, which is used to calculate the power consumption KPI of the NB-IoT RAT. A multi-mode base station may use multiple RATs including NR, LTE, NB-IoT, UMTS, and GSM. The sum of power consumption percentage of each RAT is 100 %. The larger the power consumption percentage configured for a RAT is, the larger the power consumption KPI of this RAT is.
item.name: NBIoTPercent

item.desc: This parameter sets the UMTS power consumption percentage, which is used to calculate the power consumption KPI of the UMTS RAT. A multi-mode base station may use multiple RATs including NR, LTE, NB-IoT, UMTS, and GSM. The sum of power consumption percentage of each RAT is 100 %. The larger the power consumption percentage configured for a RAT is, the larger the power consumption KPI of this RAT is.
item.name: UMTSPercent

item.desc: This parameter sets the GSM power consumption percentage, which is used to calculate the power consumption KPI of the GSM RAT. A multi-mode base station may use multiple RATs including NR, LTE, NB-IoT, UMTS, and GSM. The sum of power consumption percentage of each RAT is 100 %. The larger the power consumption percentage configured for a RAT is, the larger the power consumption KPI of this RAT is.

item.desc: This parameter sets the upper limit of the number of consecutive authentication failures. When the number of consecutive authentication failures reaches the parameter value, the user is automatically locked.
item.name: autoLockMaxRetryTimes

item.desc: This parameter sets the automatic lock type. If this parameter is set to 0 (Temporary locked), when the number of consecutive login failures reaches the upper limit,the user is locked temporarily and is unlocked automatically after a certain period of time. If this parameter is set to 1 (Permanent locked (non administrator)), when the number of consecutive login failures reaches the upper limit, if the user is not the administrator, the user is locked permanently;if the user is the administrator, the user is locked temporarily.
item.name: autoLockType

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to double the login delay. If this parameter is set to Off, when the number of consecutive login failures reaches the upper limit, the login locking duration depends on the automatic user locking duration. If this parameter is set to On, when the number of consecutive login failures reaches the upper limit, if the user is not the administrator, the login locking time is doubled based on the current automatic user locking duration; if the user is the administrator, the login locking period depends on the default value of the automatic user locking duration.
item.name: loginDoubleDelaySwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the automatic user locking duration. When the automatic locking period of a user exceeds the value, the user is automatically unlocked. Unit: minutes.
item.name: autoLockDuration

item.name: maxPwdLength

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable strong password check. If strong password check is enabled, a password must meet the following requirements: (1) The password must contain characters from the following three or four types (the number of character types is specified by the pwdCharTypeNum parameter): decimal digits, English uppercase characters, English lowercase characters, and other characters. Other characters include '! @ # $ % ^ and ( ) _ - = * ~ ` [ ] { } | : less than . greater than ?'. (2) The password must not contain the username (in the correct order or the reversed order). (3) The password must not contain three or more than three consecutive same characters (the number is specified by the prohibitedSuccSameCharsNum parameter). (4) The password must not contain three or more consecutive sequential or reverse letters or digits, for example, abc, ABC, 123, cba, CBA, or 321 (the number is specified by the maxPwdSuccessiveLetter parameter). (5) The password must not be a password in the password blacklist.
item.name: strongPwdCheckEnable

item.desc: This parameter sets the historical password repetition of a local user, that is, the new password cannot be the same as the latest N passwords (N is the value of this parameter).
item.name: pwdRepetition

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable weak dictionary check. After weak dictionary check is enabled, the passwords in the weak dictionary cannot be configured: 11111111, 12345678, password, p@ssword, iloveyou, trustno1, baseball, sunshine, passw0rd, superman, football, !@#$%^ and *, 1qaz2wsx, 1q2w3e4r, princess, and computer.
item.name: weakDicCheckEnable

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the function of deleting the default OS user on a main control board. This parameter is valid only in the PNF scenario. If this function is enabled for the first time, the procedure for deleting the default user is executed and this procedure is irreversible, that is, once the default user is deleted, the default user cannot be recovered. If this function is enabled and then disabled, the setting does not take effect and this function is immediately changed to enabled.
item.name: deleteDefaultUser

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to forbid the root user or users of the root group to log in to the main control board through SSH as the OS user. This parameter is valid only in the PNF scenario. If this parameter is set to On, the users with the root permission are forbidden to remotely log in to the main control board through SSH.
item.name: forbidRootLogin

item.desc: This parameter sets user-defined password blacklist.
item.name: pwdBlacklist

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum number of successive same characters not allowed in the password.
item.name: prohibitedSuccSameCharsNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum number of consecutive characters allowed in the password of a local user.
item.name: maxPwdSuccessiveLetter

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum number of character types allowed for the password of a local user. A password must contain characters from the following three or four types: decimal digits, English uppercase characters, English lowercase characters, and other characters.
item.name: pwdCharTypeNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the timeout time (in seconds) for an SSH session of the OS user on the main control board. This parameter is valid only in the PNF scenario. If the duration of the session between the OS user and the sshd shell remaining idle exceeds the time specified by this parameter, the session automatically exits.
item.name: sshSessionTimeout

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the GDPR function. If this parameter is set to 0 (Open), the system determines whether to desensitize the data in alarms and logs in accordance with user permissions. If this parameter is set to 1 (Close), the data in alarms and logs is not desensitized.
item.name: gdprSwitch

item.name: FDN

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the string type and can be configured as planned.
item.name: moId

item.desc: This parameter sets the username of the local user. The username must 2-20 characters consisting of uppercase letters, a lowercase letters, digits, or underscores,and the first character must be an uppercase letter or a lowercase letter. In addition, the username cannot be set to root, zte, admin, sshd, rsyslogd,, system, dockremap, pmpUser, bsaUser or syslog (neither uppercase nor uppercase form).
item.name: userName

item.desc: This parameter sets the password for the local user. There are some restrictions on the minimum and maximum length of a plaintext password.The minimum length is specified by the minPwdLength parameter of the LocalUserM configuration. The length is in the range of 8 through 20 characters.The maximum length is specified by the maxPwdLength parameter of the LocalUserM configuration. The length is in the range of 64 through 128 characters.If strong password check is enabled, a password must meet the following requirements:(1) The password must contain characters from the following three or four types (the number is specified by the pwdCharTypeNum parameter): decimal digits, English uppercase characters, English lowercase characters, and other characters. Other characters include ! @ # $ % ^ and ( ) _ - = * ~ ` [ ] { } | : less than . greater than ?.(2) The password must not contain the username (in the correct order or the reversed order).(3) The password must not contain three or more than three consecutive same characters (the number is specified by the prohibitedSuccSameCharsNum parameter).(4) The password must not contain three or more consecutive sequential or reverse letters or digits, for example, abc, ABC, 123, cba, CBA, or 321 (the number is specified by the maxPwdSuccessiveLetter parameter).(5) The password must not be a password in the password blacklist.(6) The password must not start with $0$, $5$, or $6$. If the password starts with $0$, this parameter is a plaintext parameter containing all the characters except for $0$. If the password starts with $5$ or $6$, this parameter is a ciphertext password containing all characters (for imml).(7) The password must not be a password in the weak password dictionary.
item.name: password

item.desc: This parameter sets the validity period (unit: days) of the password of a local user.
item.name: passwordActiveTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the early-warning time (unit: days) for password expiration of a local user.
item.name: advancedAlarmTime

item.desc: This parameter indicates the last password modification time.
item.name: pwdLastChangeTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the user group to which a local user belongs. The value 0 (Super Administrator User) indicates that the local user has permission to perform read, write, and execute operations on all nodes. The value 1 (Operational Administrator Users group) indicates that the local user has permission to perform read, write, and execute operations on all other nodes except for the security management node. The value 2 (Ordinary Users group) indicates that the local user cannot perform any operation on the security management node but has permission to perform only read operations on all other nodes. The value 3 (Custom Users group) indicates that the local user has all the operation code rights and the MO rights of the user roles that are associated with the local user. If no operation code is selected or no MO is allocated, this user which the user group is Custom Users group has no permission.
item.name: userGroup

item.desc: This parameter sets the type of the local user. If the user type is set to OS, the user can only log in to a main control board through SSH in the PNF scenario. If the user type is set to OAM, the user can execute only the OAM applications including link establishment between the front end and back end, WebLMT login, iMML login, and WebMNT login. If the user type is set to OAM and OS, the user can execute the OAM applications including link establishment between the front end and back end, WebLMT login, iMML login, and WebMNT login, and can log in to a main control board through SSH in the PNF scenario.
item.name: userType

item.desc: This parameter sets the user role of a local user (based on operation code). You can set a user role through the userRoleName (Name of a user role) parameter.
item.name: refUserRole

item.desc: This parameter sets the user role of a local user based on MO. You can set a user role through the userLabel (Name of a user role) parameter.
item.name: refCustomRole

item.desc: This parameter sets the certificate subject name for login. If the parameter value is null, login through the certificate fails.
item.name: subjectName

item.desc: This parameter indicates the lock status of the local user. If this parameter is set to locked, the user is locked and cannot log in to the system. When a non-administrator user is locked or unlocked, the SSH user is locked or unlocked synchronously. When the administrator is locked, the SSH administrator is not locked synchronously. The policy of preventing brute-force attack for the SSH administrator is implemented independently. SSH user locking due to operations on the SSH user is not be presented on the UME, and is guaranteed by the lock and unlock policy for the SSH user.
item.name: lockStatus

item.desc: This parameter sets the reason why a local user is locked. If a user is locked, the user is prohibited to log in to the system.
item.name: lockReason

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of consecutive login failures of a local user.
item.name: loginFailureTimes

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time for locking a local user after the local user fails in login continuously.
item.name: autoLockTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the current automatic lock duration. When the switch of doubling the login delay is set to On, this parameter determines the automatic lock duration. Unit: minutes. The parameter value is always 0 for the administrator, meaning that the parameter is not valid. When the switch of doubling the login delay is set to On, if the number of consecutive login failures reaches the upper limit, the lock duration is doubled. When the switch of doubling the login delay is set to On, if the parameter value exceeds the upper limit after being doubled, the lock duration is set to the upper limit. If the user logs in to the system successfully, the parameter is set to 0.
item.name: currentLockDuration

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum number of sessions that local users are allowed to access. It is applicable to various types of applications and takes effect independently for each application type.
item.name: maxSessionNumber

item.desc: This parameter sets the validity period (unit: days) of a local user.
item.name: userActiveTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of the user validity period.
item.name: activeStartTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of the user validity period.
item.name: activeEndTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the period (in days) during which the local user is idle, that is, the maximum number of days between this login and the last logout.
item.name: userIdlePeriod

item.desc: This parameter indicates the time when the local user logs out last time.
item.name: lastLogoutTime

item.desc: This parameter sets whether the user can execute the su command. This parameter is valid only in the PNF scenario. If this parameter is set to 1 (Off), the user is prohibited to execute the su command to switch to another username. The SSH super user can always execute the su command, and this parameter is always set to 0 (On) for the SSH user.
item.name: suEnable

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique id of the local user.
item.name: userId

item.desc: This parameter is the flag of the first successful login of the OAM local user, indicating whether the user has logged in successfully.
item.name: userFirstLoginFlag

item.desc: This parameter sets the public key. This key is used for local users to log in to the system (for example, login through the iMML). If the parameter value is null, login through public key fails.
item.name: publicKey

item.desc: This parameter sets the authentication method to be used.
item.name: authenticationMode

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to allow OAM users to log in by date. If this parameter is set to 0 (Open), OAM users are allowed to log in on the specified dates. If this parameter is set to 1 (Close), the logins of OAM users are not restricted by date.
item.name: operationLimitDateEnable

item.desc: This parameter sets the start date of the dates on which users are allowed to log in. The date format is YYYY-MM-DD. This parameter is valid only if the operationLimitDateEnable parameter is set to 0 (Open). The start date must be earlier than or equal to the end date.
item.name: operableStartDate

item.desc: This parameter sets the end date of the dates on which users are allowed to log in. The date format is YYYY-MM-DD. This parameter is valid only if the operationLimitDateEnable parameter is set to 0 (Open). The end date must be later than the start date.
item.name: operableEndDate

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to allow OAM users to log in by time. If this parameter is set to 0 (Open), OAM users are allowed to log in in a specified period. If this parameter is set to 1 (Close), the logins of OAM users are not restricted by time.
item.name: operationLimitTimeEnable

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of a period (of each day) during which users are allowed to log in. The time format is HH:MM:SS in a 24-hour system. This parameter is valid only if the operationLimitTimeEnable parameter is set to 0 (Open). The start time must be earlier than the end time.
item.name: operableStartTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of a period (of each day) during which users are allowed to log in. The time format is HH:MM:SS in a 24-hour system. This parameter is valid only if the operationLimitTimeEnable parameter is set to 0 (Open). The end time must be later than the start time.
item.name: operableEndTime

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to allow OAM users to log in by day of week. If this parameter is set to 0 (Open), OAM users are allowed to log in on specified days of each week. If this parameter is set to 1 (Close) or left unset, the logins of OAM users are not restricted by day of week.
item.name: operationLimitWeekEnable

item.desc: This parameter sets the day (of each week) on which users are allowed to log in. This parameter is valid only if the operationLimitWeekEnable parameter is set to 0 (Open).
item.name: operableWeekday

item.desc: This parameter sets the phone number of the user.
item.name: phoneNumber

item.desc: This parameter sets the email address of the user.
item.name: email

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to authenticate the mobile serial number when a user logs in to the WebLMT. If this parameter is set to 0 (Open), the function of mobile serial number verification is enabled. If this parameter is set to 1 (Close), the function is disabled.
item.name: mobileSerialNubmerSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the mobile serial number. It is used for login authentication. The mobile serial number can be found in the mobile security token app.The download address of the android version of the SafeToker APP: https://moatest.zte.com.cn/m/zte/cmcckey.apk.The download address of the iOS version of the SafeToker APP: https://moatest.zte.com.cn/m/MOATeamTrial/cmcckey.html.
item.name: pMsg_mobileSerialNumber

item.desc: This parameter sets whether the OAM user is permitted to log in to clients based on client types. If this function is enabled, the OAM user can log in to the clients of the permitted types. If this function is disabled, there is no login restriction on the client types for the OAM user.
item.name: clientTypeSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the types of clients that the OAM user is permitted to log in to. This parameter is valid only if the clientTypeSwitch parameter is set to 0 (Open).
item.name: clientTypes

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to restrict the login of the OAM user based on the IP addresses of clients in the case that the OAM user is permitted to log in to WEBLMT, IMML, or WEBMNT clients. If this function is enabled, the OAM user can log in to the clients having the permitted IP addresses. If this function is disabled, there is no login restriction on the IP addresses of clients for the OAM user.
item.name: clientIpSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the IP addresses of the clients that the OAM user is permitted to log in to. This parameter is valid only if the clientIpSwitch parameter is set to 0 (Open).
item.name: clientIpList

item.desc: This parameter specifies the domain name of the certificate issuer. It is used to fill in the subject field of the certificate issuer. It should be filled out in compliance with the X.500 standard, for example, C=**,O=**,CN=**, C means Country, O means Organization, CN means Common Name. Currently, the general format of digital certificates follows the X.509V3 international standard. A standard X.509 digital certificate contains the following information: Version information of the certificate; Serial number of the certificate(Each certificate has a unique serial number); Signature algorithm used by the certificate; Name of the certificate authority(The X.500 format is normally used as the naming scheme); Validity period of the certificate; Name of the certificate owner(The X.500 format is normally used as the naming scheme); Public key of the certificate owner; Signature of the certificate issuer.
item.name: certificateIssuerName

item.desc: This parameter sets the certificate application mode. The value 0 (ON_LINE) indicates that the certificate is obtained from the certificate server, the value 1 (OFF_LINE) indicates that the certificate is obtained locally and needs to be manually imported to the system, and the value 2 (LOCAL_ISSUE) indicates that the certificate is issued by the NE.

item.desc: This parameter sets the type of the requested certificate. The value 0 (RSA) indicates that the requested certificate is of the RSA type, and the value 2 (ECDSA) indicates that the requested certificate is of the ECDSA type.
item.name: requestCertificateType

item.desc: This parameter sets the application-layer protocol used for CMP packet transmission. The value 0 indicates the HTTP protocol, and the value 1 indicates the HTTPS protocol.
item.name: transportProtocol

item.desc: This parameter sets the TLS policy to be used when CMP packets are transmitted over TLS links. The TlsPolicy configuration indicated by this parameter is used.
item.name: refTlsPolicy

item.desc: This attribute specifies the IP address of a CA server. A CA(Certificate Authority) server processes the application request for a certificate, and issues, revokes and manages a certificate.
item.name: caServerIp

item.desc: This attribute specifies the transport-layer port number of a CA server. It should be set based on the actual configurations of the CA server.
item.name: caServerPort

item.desc: This attribute specifies the URL (the remaining part with the host address and port excluded) of the CMP protocol on the server side. It should be set based on the CMP protocol configuration of the CA server.
item.name: caServerPath

item.desc: This parameter sets the IP address of the standby Certificate Authority (CA) server. If the active CA server fails, the standby CA server is responsible for certificate application, issuing, revocation, and management.
item.name: slaveCaServerIp

item.desc: This parameter sets the transport-layer port used by the standby CA server.
item.name: slaveCaServerPort

item.desc: This parameter sets the URL (excluding the host address and port number) of the standby CA server in accordance with the CMP protocol.
item.name: slaveCaServerPath

item.desc: This parameter sets the domain name of the certificate and is used in the Subject field for certificate application. The format of the field complies with the X.509 standard, for example, C=**, O=**, CN=**, where, C indicates the country, O indicates the organization name, and CN indicates the common name. At present, certificates of standard X.509V3 are widely used. A standard X.509 digital certificate contains the following: Version information of the certificate, unique sequence number of the certificate, signature algorithm used by the certificate, name of the certificate authority (The X.500 format is normally used as the naming scheme), validity period of the certificate, name of the certificate owner (The X.500 format is normally used as the naming scheme), public key of the certificate owner, and signature of the certificate issuer.
item.name: certificateName

item.desc: This parameter sets the extended subjectAltName item of the requested certificate. The format of the item is attribute name = attribute value. For example: subjectAltName = DNS:localhost,IP:1.1.1.1.
item.name: certificateExtension

item.desc: This parameter sets the domain name of the certificate issuer and is used in the Subject field of the certificate issuer. The format of the field complies with the X.509 standard, for example, C=**, O=**, CN=**, where, C indicates the country, O indicates the organization name, and CN indicates the common name. At present, certificates of standard X.509V3 are widely used. A standard X.509 digital certificate contains the following: Version information of the certificate, unique sequence number of the certificate, signature algorithm used by the certificate, name of the certificate authority (The X.500 format is normally used as the naming scheme), validity period of the certificate, name of the certificate owner (The X.500 format is normally used as the naming scheme), public key of the certificate owner, and signature of the certificate issuer.
item.name: certificateIssuerName

item.desc: This attribute indicates the CMP authentication algorithm. The SHA1 and SHA2 algorithms are supported.
item.name: signatureAlgorithm

item.desc: This parameter sets the length of the private key in bit. For an RSA certificate, this parameter can be set to 1024, 2048, 4096, or 8192. For an ECDSA certificate, this parameter can be set to 256, 384, or 521. A digital certificate uses the public key system, that is, it uses a pair of keys that match each other for encryption and decryption. Each user sets a specific private key for decryption and signature. At the same time, a public key is configured to be shared by a group of users for encryption and signature verification. When sending a confidential file, the sender uses the receiver's public key to encrypt the file and the receiver uses his or her own private key to decrypt it. Digital encryption is an irreversible process, that is, data can be decrypted only by using the private key. Therefore, the file is transmitted securely.
item.name: privateKeyLength

item.desc: This parameter sets the reference value, which is used for authentication in message authentication code mode.
item.name: referenceValue

item.desc: This parameter sets the secret value, which is used for authentication in message authentication code mode.
item.name: pwd_secretValue

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval for periodic certificate validity detection (unit: minutes). The NE periodically detects whether the certificate is about to expire, and initiates the certificate update procedure if the certificate is about to expire.
item.name: certDetInterval

item.desc: This parameter sets the CA fingerprint. The CA fingerprint must be the same as that configured for the CA server. After the NE obtains a CA certificate, it uses the configured fingerprint algorithm to calculate the fingerprint of the CA certificate, and compares it with the fingerprint configured for the CA server. If they are the same, the NE accepts the obtained CA certificate; otherwise, the NE discards the obtained CA certificate. The format of the fingerprint value is 01:02:03, and each hexadecimal byte of the value must be concatenated by a colon. Currently, the fingerprint values can be obtained through the MD5, SHA1, and SHA256 algorithms, and the lengths of the fingerprint values calculated based on the three algorithms are 47, 59, and 95 respectively.
item.name: caFingerprint

item.desc: This parameter sets the CA identifier. A CA identifier refers to the name of a CA server that can be trusted by the NE.
item.name: caIdentifier

item.desc: This parameter sets the domain name of the certificate and is used in the Subject field for certificate application. The format of the field complies with the X.509 standard, for example, C=**, O=**, CN=**, where, C indicates the country, O indicates the organization name, and CN indicates the common name. At present, certificates of standard X.509V3 are widely used. A standard X.509 digital certificate contains the following: Version information of the certificate, unique sequence number of the certificate, signature algorithm used by the certificate, name of the certificate authority (The X.500 format is normally used as the naming scheme), validity period of the certificate, name of the certificate owner (The X.500 format is normally used as the naming scheme), public key of the certificate owner, and signature of the certificate issuer.
item.name: certificateName

item.desc: This parameter sets the extended subjectAltName item of the requested certificate. The format of the item is attribute name = attribute value. For example: subjectAltName = DNS:localhost,IP:1.1.1.1.

item.desc: This parameter sets the domain name of the certificate issuer and is used in the Subject field of the certificate issuer. The format of the field complies with the X.509 standard, for example, C=**, O=**, CN=**, where, C indicates the country, O indicates the organization name, and CN indicates the common name. At present, certificates of standard X.509V3 are widely used. A standard X.509 digital certificate contains the following: Version information of the certificate, unique sequence number of the certificate, signature algorithm used by the certificate, name of the certificate authority (The X.500 format is normally used as the naming scheme), validity period of the certificate, name of the certificate owner (The X.500 format is normally used as the naming scheme), public key of the certificate owner, and signature of the certificate issuer.
item.name: certificateIssuerName

item.desc: This parameter sets the PKCS#7 encryption algorithm. The number in the algorithm name indicates the encryption strength.
item.name: encryptionAlgorithm

item.desc: This parameter sets the hash algorithm used for PKCS#7 signature. The number in the algorithm name indicates the number of bits of the hash value. It is recommended that the SHA256 algorithm be used.
item.name: sigHashAlgorithm

item.desc: This parameter sets the digest algorithm used for the Certificate Signing Request (CSR). The number in the algorithm name indicates the number of bits of the hash value. It is recommended that SHA256 be used.
item.name: csrDigestAlgorithm

item.desc: This parameter sets the private key length of the certificate (unit: bits). This parameter is valid for only an RSA certificate. This parameter can be set to 1024, 2048, 4096, or 8192. A digital certificate uses the public key system, that is, it uses a pair of keys that match each other for encryption and decryption. Each user sets a specific private key for decryption and signature. At the same time, a public key is configured to be shared by a group of users for encryption and signature verification. When sending a piece of confidential data, the sender uses the public key of the receiver to encrypt the data and the receiver uses its private key to decrypt the data. Digital encryption is an irreversible process, that is, data can be decrypted only by using the private key. Therefore, the data is transmitted securely.
item.name: privateKeyLength

item.desc: This parameter sets the challenge password. When the CA server uses the challenge password mode to validate certificate applications, it is necessary to configure a challenge password and the challenge password must be the same as that configured on the CA server. The length of the challenge password must be less than 61.

It serves application protocols.

item.desc: This parameter sets the link disconnection tolerance time before enabling the emergency channel. If the OAM channel connected to the UME is disconnected for a duration longer than the tolerance time and the isPnpPriority parameter is set to 0 (Emergency Channel firs), the emergency channel is enabled. If the isPnpPriority is set to 1 (PNP first) and the OAM channel connected to the UME is disconnected for a duration shorter than the tolerance time, the emergency channel is enabled first. When the duration of OAM channel disconnection reaches the tolerance time, the emergency channel is disabled and the PNP is enabled.

item.desc: This parameter sets the polling period for UE selection. Currently, most measurement tools cannot measure the data of all UEs of a gNodeB. This parameter is used to track polling-based UE data collection, thus tracking the KPIs of all UEs of a gNodeB for UE status monitoring and fault identification and location. The value 0 indicates that polling-based UE data collection is disabled, and any other value indicates the polling period in seconds.
item.name: ueSelectPollingPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets a data reporting policy for Unified Data Trace (UDT). This parameter is an array parameter consisting of three elements. If element 0 is set to 1 (Open), the MR function reports data by using the new data structure to the NDS. If this element is set to 0 (Close), the MR function reports data by using the default data structure to the NDS. If element 1 is set to 1 (Open), the MR and MDT functions report combined data to the NDS. If this element is set to 0 (Close), the MR and MDT functions separately report data to the NDS. If element 2 is set to 1 (Open), the gNodeB restarts the MR task in the cast that no MR data is reported, and the MR function automatically resumes data reporting. If this element is set to 0 (Close), the MR function does not automatically resume data reporting.
item.name: udtDataRptPolicy

item.desc: This parameter sets the alarm status. It indicates the dry contact alarm switch status. The input dry contact alarm status falls into two types: normally closed alarm and normally open alarm. The output dry contact alarm status falls into two types: output low-level and output high-level. The normally closed alarm status indicates that the BBU does not receive input signals from sensors any more. The normally open alarm status indicates that the BBU always receives input signals from sensors. If an output dry contact is in output low-level status, it indicates that the link is disconnected in the output direction, and the output dry contact is unavailable. If an output dry contact is in output high-level status, it indicates that the link in the output direction is closed, and the output dry contact is available.

item.name: mainCtrlWorkMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the network backup mode for the V9200 shelf. If this parameter is set to 0 (Basic network backup), hot standby mode is enabled. If the transmission link becomes faulty, the system switches to another main control board. If this parameter is set to 1 (Intra-board network backup), the switchover of transmission links is preferentially performed on the same main control board. If all transmission links on the board become faulty, the system switches to another main control board. For example, if the main control board is configured with two transmission links and one link becomes faulty, the other link is used. If both links become faulty, the system switches to another main control board. If this parameter is set to 2 (Inter-board network backup), a transmission link is configured for each of the two main control boards. If a transmission link becomes faulty, the transmission link of the other main control board is used. If both links become faulty, the system switches to the other main control board.
item.name: networkBackupMode

item.desc: This parameter is used to indicate the energy saving mode information of the replaceable unit. The value BBU low service indicates that a BBU is in energy-saving mode with low service traffic. The value Layer 1 Device Shutdown indicates that the BBU is in low-power-consumption mode, that is, some baseband hardware is shut down to reduce power consumption. The value Layer 3 Device Shutdown indicates that on the baseband unit, the components other than the power-supply module can be shut down. Layer 3 Device Shutdown brings better energy-saving effect than Layer 1 Device Shutdown.. In all the three kinds of state, the power consumption of a BBU is reduced. The value RU deep sleep indicates that an RF unit is in in deep sleep for energy saving. The value RU carrier shutdown indicates that some frequencies are shut down for an RF unit based on service load. The value RU symbol shutdown indicates that the power amplifier of an RF unit is shut down during period without data transmission. The value RU channel shutdown indicates that RF channels are shut down based on service load. The value RU dynamic start stop indicates that an RF unit adjusts its energy saving state automatically, and most components are stopped during deep energy saving to keep the lowest power consumption. The value RU enhanced light Sleep indicates that more components for digital IF processing and transceivers are shut down based on actual data transmission for better energy saving efficiency by increasing the time for an RF unit to recover from carrier shutdown (in minute).RU enhanced light Sleep indicates that PB devices operate in deep sleep mode to reduce energy consumption.
item.name: energySavingMode

If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the RF device does not support this function, or this function is disabled on this device. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), this function is enabled. The VGA configuration can reduce interference for A9722 M1821 devices on the 2.1 GHz frequency band, thus improving uplink performance.

If an RF unit fails to be started, self-healing is not performed.

item.desc: This parameter sets the VSWR-based alarm mode. The specific value range depends on the specifications. If this parameter is set to 0, this parameter is used for the TDD RRU 8T model. If the VSWRs of three or more ports exceed the level-1 alarm threshold (specified by the upperLimit parameter of the Vswr configuration), an alarm is raised. If this parameter is set to 1, this parameter is used for the TDD RRU 8T model. As long as the VSWR of any port exceeds the level-1 alarm threshold (specified by the upperLimit parameter of the Vswr configuration), an alarm is raised. If this parameter is set to 255, the default VSWR-based alarm mode is used.
item.name: vswrAlarmMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the policy for alarm reporting in the case that the board temperature of the RF device is improper. If this parameter is set to 1 (Event), an alarm is reported immediately when the board temperature of the RF device is too high. If this parameter is set to 2 (Statistics), an alarm is reported only if the board temperature of the RF device is too high in several consecutive days and is reported when a statistical period ends.
item.name: rfTempAlarmStrategy

item.desc: This parameter set the statistical period for recording improper board temperature of the RF device for alarm reporting. This parameter is valid only if the RfDeviceConfig.rfTempAlarmStrategy parameter is set to 2 (Statistics).
item.name: rfTempAlarmStatisticsPeriod

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables functional self-rescue for RF devices. If this parameter is left blank, this function is disabled. If this parameter is set to 1 (Enabling the PA Self-Healing Function), PA self-healing is enabled. In this case, if PA self-oscillation occurs on an RF device, the self-healing procedure can be started.
item.name: functionHealingCfg

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables power configuration mode 1 for the RRU. The value 0 (Disabled) indicates that the RRU operates at the normal rated power. The value 1 (Enabled) indicates that the RRU operates at the enhanced rated power.
item.name: powerConfigMode1

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the calibration function for the antenna feeder connected to an RF port of the RRU. If this parameter is set to 0 (No), calibration is not enabled for the antenna feeder and the performance of the antenna feeder is not affected by system calibration. If this parameter is set to 1 (Yes), calibration is enabled for the antenna feeder. In this case, the system optimizes the performance of the antenna feeder through calibration, thereby improving the quality and communication stability of the radio links.
item.name: supportCalibration

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the spontaneous temperature rise function. If this parameter is set to 1 or 2, the temperature of the power chip will increase slightly during the specified period.
item.name: rfTempRiseSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the execution period of the spontaneous temperature rise function for the RF device. This parameter is valid only if the RfDeviceConfig.rfTempRiseSwitch parameter is set to 2 (Periodical spontaneous source temperature rise).
item.name: rfTempRisePeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of the execution of the spontaneous temperature rise function for the RF device. Set this parameter in the format HH:MM, for example, 3:00. The start time and end time must be configured in pairs, and the end time must be later than the start time.
item.name: rfTempRiseStartTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of the execution of the spontaneous temperature rise function for the RF device. Set this parameter in the format HH:MM, for example, 3:00. The start time and end time must be configured in pairs, and the end time must be later than the start time.
item.name: rfTempRiseEndTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the whether to enable the nighttime reset for self-healing function for the RF device. If the function is enabled, the device is reset during the night to remove the potential problems and optimize the performance-related parameter settings. To enable the function, set this parameter to 0 (Open). To disable the function, set this parameter to 1 (Close).
item.name: nightRebootHealingCfg

item.desc: This parameter sets the alarm status. It indicates the dry contact alarm switch status. The input dry contact alarm status falls into two types: normally closed alarm and normally open alarm. The output dry contact alarm status falls into two types: output low-level and output high-level. The normally closed alarm status indicates that the BBU does not receive input signals from sensors any more. The normally open alarm status indicates that the BBU always receives input signals from sensors. If an output dry contact is in output low-level status, it indicates that the link is disconnected in the output direction, and the output dry contact is unavailable. If an output dry contact is in output high-level status, it indicates that the link in the output direction is closed, and the output dry contact is available.

item.desc: This parameter sets the extended channel adjustment mode in which the extended channels of an extension box use a shared channel in the antenna pooling scenario. The value 1 indicates that the extended channels of the extension box can use the shared channel only at the scheduled time in accordance with the configured extended channel adjustment policy (whose operating mode is set by ExChannelAdjustPolicy). The value 0 indicates that the gNodeB can predict the load of each extended channel on the next day based on the historical load of each extended channel and dynamically adjust the service time of each extended channel. In addition, if no historical load data is available for prediction, the gNodeB can still use the extended channel adjustment policy.The value 2 indicates that the gNodeB can use the real-time load of each extended channel within the handover evaluation period (RruExpansionBox.loadEvaluatePeriod) and dynamically adjust each extended channel to use the shared channel.
item.name: exChannelAdjustMode

item.desc: This parameter is an array parameter consisting of three elements. These elements respectively set the first, second, and third priorities for the load indicators that are used for adjusting extended channels based on load prediction. The load indicators of the extended channels are compared in descending order of priority. If the high-priority load indicator values of the extended channels are the same, the gNodeB compares the load indicator with a lower priority.
item.name: loadPriority

item.desc: This parameter sets the evaluation period based on real-time load antenna conversion. Antenna conversion can be triggered when the load evaluation conditions are met within the period. The smaller the parameter value is, the faster the response to burst high load is, the easier it is to trigger antenna handover, but the higher the probability of incorrect handover is, and the coverage effect of the entire RF unit may be affected. The larger the parameter value is, the slower the response to burst load is, and the more difficult it is to trigger antenna switchover.
item.name: loadEvaluatePeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the replaceable unit (ReplaceableUnit) of the current clock configuration. A replaceable unit (ReplaceableUnit) of the main control device uses a clock configuration.
item.name: refReplaceableUnit

item.desc: This parameter sets how the base station synchronizes with the reference clock source. This parameter is related to the RAT type of the cell. For TDD LTE, FR1 TDD, or FR2, this parameter can be set to 1 (Phase synchronization) or 2 (Mixed synchronization). For other RAT types, all value options are supported.
item.name: clockSyncMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the clock source switching policies for the gNodeB. If the active clock source is faulty, the gNodeB switches to another clock source in accordance with this parameter. If this parameter is set to 0 (No switching), the gNodeB activates the clock source with the highest priority, and does not switch to another clock source even if this clock source is faulty. If this parameter is set to 1 (Switching by priority), the gNodeB activates the available clock source with a higher priority. If this parameter is set to 2 (Switching by status): if the clock of the gNodeB is locked, the gNodeB does not switch to another clock source of higher priority; if the clock source of the gNodeB is not locked, the gNodeB switches to another locked clock source of a higher priority.
item.name: clockSwitchPolicy

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable clock source deviation detection. If the clock source deviation detection function is enabled, when the phase deviation between the active clock source and the normal standby clock source with the highest priority exceeds the clock source deviation alarm threshold, alarm 198096830 'Too large phase difference between clock sources' is reported.
item.name: phaseDifDetEnable

item.desc: This parameter sets the alarm threshold of the deviation between the active clock source and the normal standby clock source with the highest priority. If the deviation is larger than this threshold, alarm 198096830 'Too large phase difference between clock sources larm' is reported.
item.name: difAlarmThreshold

item.desc: This parameter sets the recovery threshold of the deviation between the active clock source and the normal standby clock source with the highest priority. After alarm 198096830 'Too large phase difference between clock sources' is reported, if the deviation between the two clock sources is smaller than this threshold, the alarm is cleared.
item.name: difAlarmRecvThreshold

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the 1PPS+TOD mutual backup between BBUs. If two gNodeBs use the 1PPS+TOD clock (ClockSourcePpsTod) provided by each other as the reference clock source, this parameter should be set to 1 (Yes) for both gNodeBs. Otherwise, set this parameter to 0 (No) for them.
item.name: bbuMutualBackup

item.desc: This parameter sets the delay in reporting alarm 198092217 'System clock unavailable'. This function is valid only if clock synchronization mode is set to 1 (Phase synchronization).
item.name: airAlmDelayTime

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable holdover alarm reporting. That is, whether alarm 198096840 'System clock in holdover mode' is reported if the clock source of the gNodeB is in holdover state.
item.name: holdoverAlmEnable

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable enhanced SyncE retention. If phase synchronization mode is set for the gNodeB, if the SyncE clock (ClockSourceSyncE) meets the G.811 standard, the clock retention capability can be enhanced by setting this parameter to 1 (Yes).
item.name: synceAssisHoldEnable

item.desc: This parameter sets whether the secondary gNodeB tracks the 1PPS + TOD clock (ClockSourcePpsTod) clock of the primary gNodeB. Even if the clock source of the primary gNodeB is faulty, the clock of the secondary gNodeB still tracks the clock of the primary gNodeB.
item.name: basestationClkMSMode

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the TOD Synchronization for the NE.
item.name: todSyncEnable

item.desc: This parameter sets the benchmark clock source. When a clock source is configured as the benchmark clock source, if the gNodeB reports a 'Too large phase difference between clock sources' alarm (alarm 198096830), this clock source is activated.
item.name: benchmarkClock

item.desc: This parameter sets the radio frame offset of the NE. It is applicable to RF devices of all radio systems. If the parameter value is negative, it indicates that radio frames are sent ahead of time. If the parameter value is positive, it indicates that radio frames are sent behind time. One Tc indicates 1/3.84 microseconds.
item.name: frameOffset

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the island clock server function. If this function is enabled, lower-level base stations can synchronize their clock signals with the base station, regardless of whether this base station is connected to an external clock source or not.

item.desc: This parameter sets the fixed delay compensation value for the deviation between the gNodeB and the 1588 server.
item.name: delayCompensation

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable SyncE to assist 1588 clock synchronization. It is valid only if the Reference clock source type (ClockSource1588.clockType) parameter is set to SyncE+1588.
item.name: enableSyncE

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable SSM detection. Synchronization status information (SSM) specifies the quality level for sending timing signals through the timing synchronization link in the synchronization network. The node clock in the synchronization network obtains the parent-node clock information by reading the SSM. Operations, such as tracing and changeover, are performed on the clock of the local node, and synchronization information of the local node is sent to the subordinate nodes. This parameter can be set 1 (Yes) only if the ClockSource1588.clockType (Reference clock source type) parameter is set to 10 (SyncE+1588) and the ClockSource1588.enableSyncE (SyncE enabled) parameter is set to 1 (Yes).
item.name: isSSM

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval for switching to an available clock reference source after the current clock reference source is faulty.
item.name: switchThreshold

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the time for waiting for the 1588 clock source to be recovered. When the time during which the clock source is recovered exceeds the threshold, the clock source becomes available.
item.name: almRecoverThreshold

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the system clock to detect whether the reference clock is operating properly. If the function is enabled, the gNodeB uses the system clock to detect the 1588 reference clock to determine whether the 1588 reference clock is operating properly. This function is valid only if the clock ClockSource1588.clockType (reference source) type is set to SyncE+1588 clock.
item.name: enableSysClkDetectRef

item.desc: This parameter sets the waiting time for the base station to synchronize with the reference source time if the base station detects reference source time hopping. The default value is 0, indicating that the gNodeB does not synchronize with the reference source time. This parameter is valid only if both of the following two conditions are met: 1. The radio mode includes NB-IoT or FDD-LTE. 2. The e ClockSource1588.clockType (Reference clock source type) is set to 11 (1588 Frequency synchronization). If the gNodeB synchronizes with the time of the reference clock source that encounters time hopping hopping, FN synchronization may occur and UMTS-related services may be faulty. However, if the gNodeB does not synchronize with the time of the reference clock source that encounters time hopping hopping, HFN may fail to be corrected, affecting the functions related to NB-IoT and FDD-LTE.
item.name: todSyncTimeout

item.desc: This parameter sets the 1588 clock synchronization algorithm type.
item.name: algorithmType

item.desc: This parameter sets the user-defined traceable clock class for the base station. If the clock synchronization mode is set to 1 (Phase synchronization), this parameter can be set to only 7 (PRTC in holdover) or 135 (T-BC in holdover). There is no such restriction on other clock synchronization modes.
item.name: userDefTraceClockClass

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable detection of improper Rx optical power of the optical module of an RRU in FDD mode. item.desc: This parameter sets the operating mode of the baseband. In the case that this parameter is set to 0 (Normal mode), multiple configured baseband boards operate in load sharing mode. If a baseband board becomes faulty, services on the board will not be switched over. In the case that this parameter is set to 1 (multi-baseband redundancy mode), if a baseband board becomes faulty, services on the faulty baseband board are quickly switched over to a baseband board in normal status in the baseband pool. In the case that this parameter is set to 2 (baseband active and standby mode), only two baseband boards can be configured in the baseband pool. If the active baseband board becomes faulty, services on the active baseband board are quickly switched over to the standby baseband board.
item.name: redundancyModeSwitch

item.desc: This attribute is valid only to dual transmitting RUs. The dual transmitting RU comprises two RF channels, each of which has one main port and one diversity port. The main port has one transmitting channel (TxChannel) and one receiving channel (RxChannel). The diversity port corresponds to one RxChannel. The diversity receiving mode of dual transmitting RU can be configured as ordinary diversity reception or cross diversity reception. In the ordinary diversity reception mode, each antenna port of RU should connect to the physical antenna, and the uplink information of the diversity port of each channel comes from the connected physical antenna. When only the main antenna port (not the diversity port) of RU connects to the physical antenna, the diversity receiving mode of the dual transmitting RU can be configured as cross diversity reception. It indicates that the receiving channels of the two main antennae are diversity channels for each other and the diversity signals come from the main antenna of other channels. The cross diversity reception mode saves physical antennae for the dual transmitting RU.
item.name: diversityMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the radio frame offset mode in LTE TDD F/A bands 39/34 relative to the reference clock source. Manual: The radio frames on the air interface are offset by the value configured by the Radio frame offset mode in LTE TDD F/A bands 39/34 parameter. Automatic: The NE automatically calculates the radio frame offset on the air interface. No manual configuration is required. This mode is only applicable to scenarios where LTE TDD and TD-SCDMA co-exist. For example, in automatic mode, when the proportion between uplink and downlink of an LTE TDD cell is 2, the radio frame offset is 2688 Tc (700 microseconds) ahead of time relative to the reference clock source.

item.desc: Port aggregation processes multiple physical connections as a logical connection. Two switches can be cascaded through multiple ports and transmit data between them. Traffic can be automatically allocated on the ports, which enables load sharing. 0: Ingress Port Load. That is, the sending port is calculated in accordance with the incoming traffic load of the member ports in the LACP aggregation group for load sharing. 1: Load sharing is enabled. The transmitting ports are calculated based on the source MAC address and destination MAC address. 2: Load sharing is enabled. The transmitting ports are calculated based on the source IP address and destination IP address. For example, the base station needs to send A message (source IP address: SrclpA; destination IP address: DestIpB) and B message (source IP address: SrcIpA; destination IP address: DestIpC) to the core network. In accordance with the load sharing mode, in the aggregation group, A message is sent through one LACP member port, and message B is sent through another LACP member port. For example, the base station needs to send A message (source IP address: SrclpA; destination IP address: DestIpB) and B message (source IP address: SrcIpA; destination IP address: DestIpB) to the core network. In accordance with the load sharing mode, in the aggregation group, A and B messages are sent through the same LACP member port. The other member port in the LACP aggregation group transmits other messages so that network congestion is avoided and load sharing is enabled. 3: Load sharing is enabled. The transmitting ports are calculated based on the addresses of source TCP/UDP port and destination TCP/UDP port.
item.name: aggLoadBalance

item.desc: The working mode of an aggregation group includes the following two types: Manual mode: The LACP protocol is not enabled. All aggregate ports in the aggregation group are bundled. Static mode: The LACP protocol is enabled and used to determine the ports that can be bundled to the aggregation group. In dynamic mode, the member ports of an aggregation group may be bundled to another aggregation group. It depends on the negotiation result of the protocols on two ends.
item.name: workMode

item.desc: This attribute identifies the LACP ports contained in an aggregation group, that is, the LACP ports that are bundled into the aggregation group and be part of the link aggregation.
item.name: refLacpPort

item.desc: This parameter is used to configure the list of VLANs bound to the LACP group. If the parameter is set to 0, it indicates that the packets without VLAN information are bound to the current LACP group. If the parameter is set to a value in the range of [1, 4094], it indicates that the packets with the corresponding VLAN information are bound to the current LACP group.
item.name: vlanList

item.desc: This parameter sets the pRRU power-off mode for energy saving. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), pRRU powering off for energy saving is not enabled. If this parameter is set to 1 (Timing mode), pRRUs are powered off at scheduled time points for energy saving. If this parameter is set to 2 (Point Control Mode), some sentinel pRRUs for traffic monitoring are not powered off, and other powered-off pRRUs are woken up as needed.
item.name: savingMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the list of pRRUs not configured with the power-off policy for energy saving. This parameter is valid when the pRRU ES policy parameter (savingPolicy) is set to 0 (eNodeB-Level Saving Policy).
item.name: refReplaceableUnit

item.desc: This parameter sets the list of sentinel pRRUs for traffic monitoring for the precisely-controlled power-off function. The NE can automatically wake up the powered-off non-sentinel pRRUs based on the traffic reported by the sentinel pRRUs. This parameter is valid if the savingMode (Power-off mode for energy saving) parameter is set to 2 (Point Control Mode) and the savingPolicy (pRRU ES policy) parameter is set to 1 (Device-Level Saving Policy).
item.name: refSentinelPrruList

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of energy saving on weekdays (from Monday to Friday). This parameter is valid when the pRRU ES policy parameter (savingPolicy) is set to 0 (eNodeB-Level Saving Policy). It must be set in the format of HH:MM, for example, 8:00. The start time and end time of energy saving on weekdays must be configured in pairs. If the start time and end time are the same, it indicates that energy saving is disabled. If the start time is later than the end time, it indicates that the energy saving period crosses days.
item.name: weekdayStartTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of energy saving on weekdays (from Monday to Friday). This parameter is valid when the pRRU ES policy parameter (savingPolicy) is set to 0 (eNodeB-Level Saving Policy). It must be set in the format of HH:MM, for example, 8:00. The start time and end time of energy saving on weekdays must be configured in pairs. If the start time and end time are the same, it indicates that energy saving is disabled. If the start time is later than the end time, it indicates that the energy saving period crosses days.
item.name: weekdayEndTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of energy saving on weekends (Saturday and Sunday). This parameter is valid when the pRRU ES policy parameter (savingPolicy) is set to 0 (eNodeB-Level Saving Policy). It must be set in the format of HH:MM, for example, 8:00. The start time and end time of energy saving on weekends must be configured in pairs. If the start time and end time are the same, it indicates that energy saving is disabled. If the start time is later than the end time, it indicates that the energy saving period crosses days.
item.name: weekendStartTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of energy saving on weekends (Saturday and Sunday). This parameter is valid when the pRRU ES policy parameter (savingPolicy) is set to 0 (eNodeB-Level Saving Policy). It must be set in the format of HH:MM, for example, 8:00. The start time and end time of energy saving on weekends must be configured in pairs. If the start time and end time are the same, it indicates that energy saving is disabled. If the start time is later than the end time, it indicates that the energy saving period crosses days.
item.name: weekendEndTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the pRRU power-off policy for energy saving. If this parameter is set to 0 (eNodeB-Level Saving Policy), it indicates that the base station-level pRRU energy saving policy is enabled, the pRRUs not participating in energy saving (PrruSavingArray.refReplaceableUnit) need to be configured, and the pRRUs participating in energy saving use the same energy saving configuration. If this parameter is set to 1 (Device-Level Saving Policy), it indicates that the device-level pRRU energy saving policy is enabled. The pRRUs participating in energy saving (PrruSavingArray.refReplaceableUnit) need to be configured, and different pRRUs may have different energy saving configurations.
item.name: savingPolicy

item.desc: This parameter sets the difference between the highest temperature and the lowest temperature of a board. Before the pRRU is powered off for energy saving, the pRRU needs to determine whether the maximum temperature difference of a board within 24 hours is larger than the parameter value. If yes, the pRRU cannot be powered off for energy saving.
item.name: deltaTLimit

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval between two handshake messages. For example, if this parameter is set to 1, it indicates that a handshake packet is sent every 100 ms. item.desc: This parameter sets the level of the Maintenance Domain (MD). The value range is 0-7, corresponding to the MD level planned for the Connectivity Fault Management (CFM) function in the existing network. This parameter can be configured as planned. The CFM function enables active fault diagnosis for point-to-point or multipoint-to-multipoint Ethernet Virtual Connections (EVCs). CFM is the core function of the IEEE 802.1ag/Y.1731 protocol for detecting end-to-end service level Ethernet faults.
item.name: mdLevel

item.desc: This parameter sets the Maintenance Domain (MD) name. Only the following characters can be used in the MD name: 0-9, a-z, A-Z, !#$% and '()*+,-./@:;less than or equal togreater than?`[]^_{|}~, and space (The space cannot appear at the beginning and end of the MD name). It is recommended that you use the MD name planned for the CFM function of the existing network. Note: The number of characters of the MD name of the MD object + the number of characters of any MA name associated with the MA object of this MD object less than or equal to 43.
item.name: mdName

When a user configures a Maintenance Point (MP) object, the user must specify the MA object associated with the specified MP. Each Maintenance Domain (MD) can be configured with a maximum of 4 MAs. The MA index IDs of different MDs can be the same.
item.name: maIndex

item.name: vid

item.desc: This parameter sets the Maintenance Association (MA) name. Only the following characters can be used in the MD name: 0-9, a-z, A-Z, !#$% and '()*+,-./@:;less than or equal togreater than?`[]^_{|}~, and space (The space cannot appear at the beginning and end of the MD name). This parameter corresponds to the Maintenance Domain (MD) name planned for Connectivity Fault Management (CFM) in the existing network. This parameter is configured as planned. The total number of characters of the MA name and the name of the associated MD cannot exceed 43 bytes.
item.name: maName

item.desc: This parameter sets the time interval between Continuity Check Message (CCM) detections. CCM detection is used to detect connectivity by sending CCM packets. The CFM link refers to the link between MEPs in an MA defined in the 802.1ag/Y.1731 protocol. CFM is a concept defined in the 802.1ag/Y.1731 protocol. The 802.1ag/Y.1731 protocol allows to define multiple MDs, each MD has multiple MAs, each MA has multiple MEPs, and there is a CFM link between two MEPs. In this way, multiple CFM links to be detected by CCM can be defined. According to the configured time interval between detections, detection packets are sent to the peer Maintenance association End Point (MEP). If no correct CCM message is received from the peer end after 3.5 times of the time interval, it is considered that the Connectivity Fault Management (CFM) link between the local MEP and the peer MEP is abnormal. These time intervals are defined in the IEEE 802.1ag/Y.1731 protocol. The interval of 3.3 ms and the interval of 10 ms are not supported for the time being. Note: The smaller the time interval is the larger the number of packets are sent, and the capability of sending and receiving packets is affected. It is recommended that you set the time interval as long as possible in accordance with the network plan. The longer the time interval, the slower the network fault detection.
item.name: ccmPeriod

item.name: mepFullNetNo

item.desc: This parameter sets the Maintenance association End Point (MEP) type. This parameter can be set to local MEP or remote MEP. In the same associated Maintenance Association (MA) object, only one local MEP object can be configured, but multiple remote MEP objects can be configured, and each remote MEP object must be associated with the local MEP object configured in the same associated MA object. It is recommended that you configure the local MEP first, and then add the remote MEPs and associate them with the configured local MEP.

item.desc: This parameter indicates the MAC address of the remote MEP in the detailed remote MEP configuration, separated by colons, for example, 00:AA:BB:88:99:DD.
item.name: remoteMEPMacAddr

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable Continuity Check Message (CCM) detection. The CCM detection method is described as follows: An MP periodically sends CCM packets to other MPs in the same MD (that is, the same VLAN of the same level) and also receives CCM packets from other MPs. CCM detection can be implemented by using unicast packets or multicast packets. When a Maintenance association End Point (MEP) is a local MEP, enabling CCM detection indicates performing multicast CCM detection at the local end. When an MEP is a remote MEP, enabling CCM detection indicates performing unicast CCM detection at the remote end. For the remote MEP and local MEP in the same MA, CCM detection cannot be enabled at the same time.
item.name: enableCCMDetect

If this function is enabled, in the case that a hardware device of the gNodeB is replaced, the UME automatically obtains the information about the new hardware device and updates the configuration related to the new hardware device, thus avoiding inconsistency between the configuration on the UME and the hardware device. If this function is disabled, the UME cannot automatically update its local configuration after the replacement of a hardware device. In this case, you need to manually modify the configuration on the UME.

item.desc: This parameter sets the fan speed adjustment mode of the cabinets of the NE. In normal mode, the fans in the cabinets are operating in accordance with cabinet configuration. In time period mode, the fans in all cabinets use the same policy. Within the configured time period, the fans in all cabinets are operating in high heat-dissipation performance mode. Beyond the configured time period, the fans in all cabinets are operating in low noise mode.

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of the first time period. This parameter is valid when the fan speed adjustment mode is set to 1 (Time period mode), and the parameter value must be later than the start time. The start time and end time of different time periods cannot overlap. The parameter value ranges from 0 to 24 (0:00-24:00) on the hour.
item.name: time1Start

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of the first time period. This parameter is valid when the fan speed adjustment mode is set to 1 (Time period mode), and the parameter value must be later than the start time. The start time and end time of different time periods cannot overlap. The parameter value ranges from 0 to 24 (0:00-24:00) on the hour.
item.name: time1End

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of the second time period. This parameter is valid when the fan speed adjustment mode is set to 1 (Time period mode), and the parameter value must be later than the start time. item.name: time2Start

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of the second time period. This parameter is valid when the fan speed adjustment mode is set to 1 (Time period mode), and the parameter value must be later than the start time. item.name: time2End

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of the third time period. This parameter is valid when the fan speed adjustment mode is set to 1 (Time period mode), and the parameter value must be later than the start time. The start time and end time of different time periods cannot overlap. The parameter value ranges from 0 to 24 (0:00-24:00) on the hour.
item.name: time3Start

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of the third time period. The start time and end time of different time periods cannot overlap. The parameter value ranges from 0 to 24 (0:00-24:00) on the hour.
item.name: time3End

If the parameter is set to 1 (Master), it indicates that the software on the shared device needs to get updates from the local NE, in other words, when the software on the local NE is upgraded, the software on the shared device is also upgraded. If the parameter is set to 0 (Slave), it indicates that when the software on the local NE is upgraded, the software on the shared RF device is not upgraded.

In the separate-BBU networking mode, the active NE is responsible for O and M, and you need to configure the interconnection port. In the scenario where two BBUs are deployed in redundancy mode, logical signaling channels are established between the shared device and the active device, and between the shared device and the standby NE.

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of energy saving on working days (Monday to Friday). The parameter must be set in accordance with the required format HH:MM, for example 8:00. Both the start time and end time of energy saving on working days must be set. If the start time is the same as the end time, energy saving is not enabled. The duration between the start time and end time can be longer than 24 hours (one day).
item.name: weekdayStartTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of energy saving on working days (Monday to Friday). The parameter must be set in accordance with the required format HH:MM, for example 8:00. Both the start time and end time of energy saving on working days must be set. If the start time is the same as the end time, energy saving is not enabled. The duration between the start time and end time can be longer than 24 hours (one day).
item.name: weekdayEndTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of energy saving on weekends (Saturday and Sunday). The parameter must be set in accordance with the required format HH:MM, for example 8:00. Both the start time and end time of energy saving on weekends must be set. If the start time is the same as the end time, energy saving is not enabled. The duration between the start time and end time can be longer than 24 hours (one day).
item.name: weekendStartTime
